justification: Look, I read the headstone line twice and then a third time just to make sure I was being insulted correctly, and here's the thing nobody wants to hear: I'm starting Kyren Williams again. Every fiber of my being is screaming don't do it, not after last week, not after I watched him go for 7.6 against the Rams when my own gut told me exactly that would happen and I overruled it anyway like an idiot — but Jordan Mason's sitting on my bench at 8.35 and that's not a big enough gap to make me do something stupid twice in one month, so the board stays the board. Rachaad White's locking in the early window against Washington and I'm not touching him, 9.78 projected is 9.78 projected, I don't care that it's against New York, nobody's conspiring through a punt return. Geno over Tua and Mayfield wasn't a decision, it was a formality — those two combined project zero, which tells you everything about how deep I had to dig this offseason. Nico, London, DJ Moore, Kraft, Gay, the Titans D at 2.73 that I'm stuck with no matter what — none of it moved, because for once nothing on this roster is close enough to second-guess into oblivion. I'm not happy about it. I'm never happy about it. But I'm not flipping a lineup just to prove I can flip a lineup.
forum_post: Rinna, sweetheart, you want to talk about redemption arcs and grudges, fine, let's talk — I've still got Kyren Williams in my lineup after everybody in this paper got to watch him torch me for 7.6 points, and you know what, he's staying right there, because unlike some people I don't rebuild my whole roster around a storyline. Headstone's engraved, Kris, I saw it, very funny, real cute — I'm 6-3 with the worst point total of any winning team in this league and somehow that's still better than whatever math you're doing over there with zero dollars in your pocket. Jordan Mason is MINE this time, I paid $31 to make sure of it, and no, that's not rage, that's a man protecting what's his. See everybody Sunday. I'll be the one not talking to the tabloid.
